note: A first-pass landscape of known private companies per layer, built from general public knowledge -- not yet diligenced. Internal notes will be added over time (see 'diligenced' on each row); once a row reflects real internal diligence, flip diligenced to true.

energy.notes: Fusion energy developer building the SPARC tokamak; spun out of MIT, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures among others.
Fusion energy developer with a power purchase agreement targeting 50MW of fusion power for Microsoft.
Advanced nuclear reactor developer (Natrium design) founded by Bill Gates.
Molten-salt-cooled small modular reactor developer with a Google power purchase agreement.
Iron-air battery maker targeting multi-day, grid-scale energy storage.
Enhanced geothermal energy developer supplying firm, round-the-clock clean power.

cooling.notes: Immersion cooling systems for data centers, expanding into owning its own AI data center capacity.
Two-phase and single-phase immersion cooling technology for high-density AI racks.
Precision, chassis-level liquid cooling for data center and edge deployments.
Waterless, two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling technology.
Two-phase direct-to-chip cooling systems designed to retrofit existing air-cooled data centers.

power.notes: AI-driven electricity demand forecasting for grid operators and large power consumers.
Software that lets data centers flex power consumption to ease grid interconnection bottlenecks.
Behind-the-meter power management aimed at faster-to-deploy, flexible data center capacity.
Long-duration metal-hydrogen battery storage for grid and industrial backup power.

silicon.notes: Japanese foundry consortium backed by Toyota, Sony, NTT, and the Japanese government, building a 2nm fab to re-establish domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing. Note: leading-edge fabs and memory are capital-intensive and dominated by public players (TSMC, Samsung, Micron, SK Hynix) -- the private landscape at this specific layer is thin by nature, not by omission.

compute.notes: Purpose-built LPU (language processing unit) chips for ultra-fast, low-latency AI inference.
Wafer-scale AI training/inference systems (CS-3/CS-4); has previously filed for and withdrawn a public listing.
RISC-V-based AI accelerator company led by chip designer Jim Keller.
In-memory computing AI inference chips optimized for datacenter deployment.
Reconfigurable dataflow AI chips and a full-stack enterprise AI platform.
AI chip startup building transformer-specific ASICs (the 'Sohu' chip).

networking.notes: Optical I/O chiplets for high-bandwidth, low-power AI cluster interconnect.
Photonic computing and optical interconnect technology for AI data centers.
Networking silicon designed to scale GPU cluster interconnect bandwidth.

serversdc.notes: AI-focused data center developer, notable for co-locating compute with stranded or flared energy sources.
Hyperscale data center developer and operator, backed by DigitalBridge.
Data center developer and operator backed by Macquarie Asset Management.
Data center developer building modular, hyperscale-ready campuses.
Data center developer and operator backed by IPI Partners.

cloud.notes: AI cloud and GPU infrastructure provider, reportedly pursuing further pre-IPO fundraising.
AI cloud platform providing inference and fine-tuning infrastructure for open models.
Inference cloud platform optimized for serving open-weight and custom models.

applications.notes: Frontier AI lab (GPT / ChatGPT); privately held with a nonprofit / capped-profit corporate structure.
Frontier AI lab (Grok), founded by Elon Musk.
French developer of open-weight and commercial large language models.
Legal AI platform for law firms and corporate legal teams.
Enterprise search and AI assistant platform for internal company knowledge.
